blocks.prompt: 13. If the lines \(2x + 3y - 7 = 0\), \(4x - y - 5 = 0\) and \(6x + ay - 9 = 0\) meet at a point, then find the value of \(a\).
blocks.explanation:
'Ek point par milti hain' ka matlab hai lines concurrent hain; sawal ne lafz badal diya hai, baat wohi hai.
Teesri line mein na-maloom \(a\) hai.
Theorem 3 se determinant zero rakhenge to \(a\) ki equation milegi.
Plan: determinant \(= 0\), \(a\) hal karna, aur meeting point se tasdeeq.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(2x + 3y - 7 = 0\), \(4x - y - 5 = 0\), \(6x + ay - 9 = 0\) concurrent hain.
Maloom karna: \(a\).
Tareeqa: Theorem 3; determinant ko zero ke barabar rakh kar \(a\) hal karna.
Pehli do lines mein koi na-maloom nahi, is liye un ka meeting point pakka hai; a ki value aisi chahiye ke teesri line bhi usi point se guzre.

Determinant banayein
\[\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 3 & -7 \\ 4 & -1 & -5 \\ 6 & a & -9 \end{vmatrix} = 0\]
Kyun: concurrent lines ka determinant zero hona zaroori hai; is se \(a\) ki ek equation milegi.
Har row ek line ke \(a, b, c\) hain; \(a\) teesri row mein doosri jagah aaya kyunke woh \(y\) ka coefficient hai.

Pehli row ke saath expand karein
\[2(9 + 5a) - 3(-36 + 30) - 7(4a + 6) = 0\]
\[18 + 10a + 18 - 28a - 42 = 0\]
\[-6 - 18a = 0\]
Kyun: pehli row par signs \(+, -, +\); har \(2 \times 2\) minor \(ps - qr\) hai.
Dhyan dein: beech wale term ka minus sign aksar choot jata hai.

Hal karein
\[18a = -6\]
\[a = -\dfrac{1}{3}\]
Kyun: yeh \(a\) ki seedhi linear equation hai.
Fraction wala jawab dekh kar ghabrayen nahi; a = minus ek tihai bilkul sahi hai, answer key (number 16) bhi yahi deti hai.

Tasdeeq:
Pehli do lines \(\left(\frac{11}{7}, \frac{9}{7}\right)\) (\(y = 4x - 5\) rakhne se: \(14x - 22 = 0\)) par milti hain. Teesri line mein rakhein:
\[6\left(\tfrac{11}{7}\right) - \tfrac{1}{3}\left(\tfrac{9}{7}\right) - 9 = \tfrac{66 - 3 - 63}{7} = 0\]
Teesri line bhi isi point se guzarti hai, jawab sahi hai.
